invariants.name: A hook-skip push passes only with a green gate record of its source
Each work-loss denial names a change that git discards

abstraction.hides: The fd of each redirect, the count of stdin sources, the unknown $ forms, the git config of the environment, the profile blob of the gate record and the bytes of each hook in a core.hooksPath folder.
callersKnow: parseShell marks stdin dynamic for each source other than one quoted heredoc, one static here-string or one whole pipe stage, so shellSteps marks such a shell step stdin.
parseShell marks a word with an unknown $ form dynamic and splitting, and it reads $"..." as a double-quoted string.
The destructive handler gives the hook-skip reason for each git config of the environment that can turn the hooks off.
A hook-skip push passes only when the gate record of its source holds the profile blob of the source and of its merge base with the record base.
abstraction.deletionTest: Without the fd and stdin source count, bash < f and bash 0<<'EOF' read as a shell with no script. Without the profile blob, a commit that drops a gate gets a record.

alternatives.name: A boundary against a hostile agent
alternatives.rejectedBecause: It needs an OS sandbox, and the guards stop agent mistakes (ADR 0011 D6).

alternatives.name: A list of literal $ forms only
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Each unknown form then reads as a static word, as $"pr" did.

alternatives.name: A signed gate record
alternatives.rejectedBecause: The agent owns the key and the state folder.

omitted: The model takes the plain form of each shell step and the hook-skip read as true observations. The parser tests and the guard rows examine them.
The model does not show that the TypeScript code refines it. The conformance test and the guard rows examine that relation.

bounds: Attended and unattended sessions, four base authorities, three working-tree authorities, two PRs, two channels, a guard error or none, and prompts of one or two of seven clause classes from four sources.
Each combination of four path facts for one write and an optional commit.
Each set of changes from four change kinds in three places, and 16 git commands with their documented effects.
One repo at the path that the session makes, one record of that path, its settle window, and a repo of another process that appears after the window.
A HEAD whose gates pass or fail under the base profile or an edited profile, one gate run, and one push or commit with or without a hook skip to three targets.

negative.defect: The destructive guard passes a hook-skip push whose gate record holds another profile blob than the source and its merge base, so a push under an edited profile skips the git hooks.

limits: The guards stop agent mistakes and are no security boundary. A variable that hides a path or a name keeps its verdict.
The agent can write the state folder with a tool that the hook does not read, so the gate record is a mistake guard.
The finite model takes the plain form, the hook-skip read and the profile compare as true observations.
Exact-head CI, review and every ordinary gate stay required.
